structure.title: A remembered conversation
structure.text: Phaedo recounts Socrates' last day. The prison setting holds a series of arguments about death and the soul.

structure.title: Objection and response
structure.text: Friends challenge the arguments, forcing distinctions between a consoling belief and a defensible explanation. The final scene returns argument to bodily experience.

context.title: Body and soul
context.text: The dialogue examines whether the soul is separable from bodily life. It offers several arguments rather than treating survival as already demonstrated.

context.title: Forms
context.text: References to equality, beauty, and other stable objects of thought support claims about knowledge and the soul. These are philosophical proposals, not ordinary visible things.
context.takeaway: Ask what the proposed object explains.

notice.why: Friendship can make intellectual honesty emotionally difficult.
The conversation uses different kinds of reassurance.

opening: Socrates' friends arrive at the prison knowing he will die that day. He wants to discuss whether death should frighten them, and whether the soul can survive the body. They listen, object, and worry that affection is making them too willing to believe him. Plato places an argument about immortality beside the immediate business of losing a friend. Every objection carries two pressures at once: the need for an answer that holds up, and the wish that it might offer consolation before time runs out.
